text.p: Kuoni Reisen Holding AG plans more acquisitions to expand in the fast-growing travel sector, where, according to chief executive Riccardo Gullotti, a new job will be created every 2.4 seconds over the next 10 years.
Kuoni, based in Switzerland, took a 51 percent stake in Indian travel firm SOTC Holidy Tours last September, one of roughly 10 acquisitions last year.
Gullotti, speaking at a news briefing to present 1996 results, said Kuoni is now close to finalising an agreement with an Asian partner. He declined to elaborate.
"Negotiations with a significant partner in Asia are close to being completed," Gullotti said.
The company is by no means done with expansion.
"Given the fact that we have reached and exceeded our goals, one should not conclude that we regard our restructuring, expansion and growth as completed. Our work has just begun," Gullotti said.
In an interview with Reuters T.V., he said Kuoni has made good "organic growth" in countries like Spain and Italy.
"But we intend to add acquisitions to this, first in the countries where we are already represented, but also in new countries," he said.
The company reported revenues in 1996 of 3.5 billion Swiss francs, up from 2.9 billion in 1995. Around half of the increase in revenues was due to acquisitions.
Max Katz, director of finance, said at the news briefing Kuoni will begin in 1997 to activate goodwill from acquisitions and the process will likely continue for a period of 10 years.
The move was in line with its plans to conform with international accounting standard guidelines.
Such write-offs reflect the difference between the price paid for an acquired company and its tangible assets.
The decision to do the write-offs would not affect plans for further acquisitions.
"We will activate the goodwill starting in 1997 and do write-offs for 10 years... and we will continue to make acquisitions. That is exactly what they (our shareholders) want," Gullotti said.

The company reported in March that its group net profit rose to 69.4 million Swiss francs in 1996 from 45.2 million in 1995. It said that first quarter 1997 results were above expectations, leading it to expect double-digit growth in revenues for the entire year.
It expected an increase in its EBIT (Earnings Before Interest and Tax) of 20 percent or more this year.
It said that depending on developments on securities exchanges, which affect its financial result, the concern profit should also improve in line with that.
